# 美股周评 · 2026-10-03：市场进入防御，AI 硬件保持强势

RI-WR-2026-W40 · v1.0 · 作者 Sunny · 发布 2026-10-03 · 主要数据截至 2026-10-02

## 本期判断

截至 10 月 2 日，综合市场状态为 66.8，进入防御区间。10 月 2 日周频信号为 Level 5，对应 35% 参考风险敞口，10 月 5 日生效。SMH 近 20 个交易日上涨 14.12%，AI 硬件评分为 91.5；板块强势与整体市场防御并存。

## 整体防御，局部强势

本周的分化很直观：按冻结的价格记录，SPY 近 5 个交易日下跌 0.22%，QQQ 上涨 0.68%，SMH 上涨 3.96%。半导体相对领先，但这种领先尚不能代表整个市场。[1][2]

当前版本的综合分数从 9 月 25 日的 63.77 升至 10 月 2 日的 66.82，由谨慎进入防御。参与度风险为 75.0，脆弱性为 92.6；金融压力为 36.0，仍属中性。风险主要体现为股票内部结构的薄弱，而不是这组指标已经确认了融资危机。[1]

10 月 2 日生成的周频信号为 Level 5，参考风险敞口 35%，有效日为 10 月 5 日。这是模型输出，不是作者实际持仓，也不是未来回报预测。整体市场状态与 AI 硬件强势应分别观察，不能因局部上涨而忽略整体风险。[1]

## 37% 到底表示什么

截图首页的 37.0% 是两项月度广度指标的简单均值：9 月末站上 200 日均线的比例为 41.47%（2,446 / 5,898）；近 12 个月跑赢标普代理 SPY 的比例为 32.60%（1,863 / 5,715）。均值为 37.04%，并不等于站上 200 日均线的比例。[1]

10 月 2 日的日频 200DMA 估算为 42.03%（2,449 / 5,827）。月末与日频样本分母不同，不能将 37% 到 42% 写成同一指标改善了 5 个百分点。两项月度数据来自 Massive 扩展，不冒称 CRSP 官方月度值；日频值单独列为估算。[1]

## AI 硬件：强势，也偏热

AI 硬件综合分数为 91.5，状态为 Strong。需求动量 100.0、供应链确认 95.4、相对风险偏好 90.4，说明模型中的强势有多个维度支持。SMH 近 20 个交易日上涨 14.12%，同期 QQQ 上涨 4.45%、SPY 下跌 0.46%；SMH 分别领先 9.67 和 14.57 个百分点。[1][2]

28 只监测股票中，25 只站上 20 日均线，25 只站上 50 日均线，均为 89.3%。这里是板块样本的短、中期均线广度，不是全市场 200 日均线广度。近 20 日相对领先的包括 AMD、TER、MRVL，涨幅约为 39.0%、32.6%、30.4%。[1]

拥挤与热度为 81.5，分化脆弱性为 69.6。前四项支柱越高越强，后两项越高则风险越大，图表用不同颜色区分。综合分数处在高位，不意味着入场成本低或上涨会持续；接下来更值得看的是强势能否扩散，以及热度和分化是否回落。[1]

## 长端利率：一个月与三个月给出的答案不同

截至 10 月 1 日，ACM 10 年期拟合收益率为 5.217%，由预期平均短端利率分项 4.312% 与期限溢价 0.905% 构成。这是模型分解，不是市场成交报价；预期分项也不等于下一次 FOMC 的政策利率预测。[3]

9 月 1 日至 10 月 1 日，拟合收益率上升 34.99 bp，其中预期分项贡献 22.42 bp，期限溢价贡献 12.58 bp，预期分项占约 64%。一个月窗口中，未来利率路径的重新定价贡献较多；期限溢价也在上升，不能忽略。[3]

三个月窗口则不同：总变化 68.93 bp，预期分项为 32.70 bp，期限溢价为 36.23 bp，后者略占多数。六个月和一年窗口的预期分项再次占主导。因此，不能把三个月至一年的所有窗口都归结为利率预期。长端上行可能增加估值压力，但本报告未识别它对股票回报的独立因果影响。[3]

## 金融条件与下周观察

最新可用 NFCI 为 -0.548，ANFCI 为 -0.574，日期为 9 月 25 日，两者均低于零，表示各自口径下金融条件较长期均值宽松。差值 0.026 不能单独当作金融条件已经收紧的证据。金融压力支柱为中性，与股市结构风险偏高可以同时成立。[1][4]

下周重点看三件事：日频 200DMA 广度能否与价格一起改善；参与度风险和脆弱性是否回落；AI 硬件的供应链、板块广度能否保持，同时拥挤与分化降温。单看某一天指数上涨，还不足以判定综合状态已经改善。

## 数据与方法

本期发布日期为 2026-10-03，股票及模型主要截止日为 2026-10-02；ACM 截止 2026-10-01，NFCI / ANFCI 截止 2026-09-25。所有表格与图形均由本期冻结输入生成。附带的数据文件提供本报告使用的数值，不含本地数据库路径或账户凭据。

综合状态使用四支柱的历史滚动分位与等权口径：低于 35 为建设性，35 至低于 50 为中性，50 至低于 65 为谨慎，65 至低于 80 为防御，80 及以上为压力。分数不是危机发生概率。旧版加权分数 60.3 与本期正式分数 66.8 不是同一口径。

本期周度比较使用同一冻结版本：9 月 25 日综合分数 63.77，10 月 2 日为 66.82。已发表的上一期报告为历史版本，分数 63.36；两者有重算差异。本期没有改写旧报告，不把修订差异当成市场变化。

价格变化来自 dashboard 的 5 日和 20 日复权价格字段，未独立重建分红再投资，不称为策略回报。全市场月度广度覆盖率分别约为 92.3% 和 91.7%，样本分母会变化。AI 硬件样本仅有 28 只监测股票，不能代表全部科技股。

因子拥挤的数据日期并不一致：多空无市场项截至 9 月 30 日；多头经 beta 调整项截至 8 月 31 日。本期不把它们写成同日新信号。截图中标到 10 月 31 日的独立 WQS 读数不作为已实现的当期观测引用；综合状态原值按导出保留，未重新计算该模型。

封面沿用用户提供的原图，曲线是封面装饰，不作为真实历史走势；正文图表均为冻结数据绘制。模型资料及后续历史可能修订，报告保存本期版本。

## 披露

本材料由 Residual Inertia | 余势制作，作者 Sunny，仅供研究与信息交流，不构成投资或证券交易建议。参考风险敞口不代表实际账户仓位。历史表现不保证未来结果；作者实际持仓及利益冲突信息未在本报告中披露。

## Broad-market risk and sector strength
In the frozen dashboard data, five-trading-day price changes were -0.22% for SPY, +0.68% for QQQ and +3.96% for SMH. The same-vintage composite score rose from 63.77 on September 25 to 66.82 on October 2, moving from Caution to Defensive. Participation risk was 75.0, fragility 92.6, market risk 63.7 and financial stress 36.0. The October 2 weekly signal is Level 5 with a 35% reference exposure, effective October 5. These are model readings, not the author's holdings.[1][2]

## What the 37.0% breadth figure means
The dashboard home figure is the simple mean of two September month-end ratios: 41.47% above the 200-day moving average (2,446/5,898) and 32.60% outperforming the SPY benchmark proxy over 12 months (1,863/5,715). Their average is 37.04%. The October 2 daily 200DMA estimate is separately 42.03% (2,449/5,827). The monthly figures use the Massive extension; they are not described as official CRSP observations. Different metrics and denominators prevent treating 37% to 42% as a five-point improvement.[1]

## AI hardware: strong, with heat and divergence
The composite scored 91.5 (Strong), with demand momentum 100.0, supply-chain confirmation 95.4, leadership breadth 81.2 and relative risk appetite 90.4. Crowding/heat at 81.5 and divergence fragility at 69.6 are risk measures, so higher is worse. SMH's 20-trading-day gain of 14.12% exceeded QQQ's 4.45% and SPY's -0.46% by 9.67 and 14.57 percentage points. In the 28-stock monitored universe, 25 stocks were above each of the 20-day and 50-day averages (89.3%). These are sector measures, not broad-market 200DMA breadth. AMD, TER and MRVL led the monitored universe over 20 days, gaining approximately 39.0%, 32.6% and 30.4%. A high composite score does not imply a low entry cost or continuing gains. Watch whether strength spreads as heat and divergence ease.[1][2]

## Rates: the answer depends on the window
As of October 1, the ACM 10-year fitted yield was 5.217%, comprising a 4.312% expected-average-short-rate component and a 0.905% term premium. Between September 1 and October 1, it rose 34.99 bp: 22.42 bp from the expected-rate component and 12.58 bp from the premium. Over three months, the premium contributed slightly more (36.23 bp versus 32.70 bp; total 68.93 bp). The expected-rate component accounted for approximately 64% of the one-month change; the term premium also rose. Rising long-end rates may increase valuation pressure, but this report does not identify an independent causal effect on equity returns. Expected rates contributed more over six months (60.33 versus 22.41 bp) and one year (75.90 versus 29.32 bp). These are model decompositions, not traded yield quotes or forecasts of the next FOMC decision.[3]

## Financial conditions and what to watch
The latest available NFCI and ANFCI observations, dated September 25, were -0.548 and -0.574. Both indicate looser-than-average conditions under their respective definitions; their 0.026 difference alone does not establish tightening.[1][4] Watch whether daily breadth improves alongside prices, participation and fragility ease, and AI hardware strength persists while heat and divergence cool.

## Version, methods and limitations
Published October 3, 2026. Equity/model cutoff: October 2; ACM: October 1; NFCI/ANFCI: September 25. The composite uses the dashboard's four-pillar rolling-percentile/equal-weight method; thresholds are <35 Constructive, 35-<50 Neutral, 50-<65 Caution, 65-<80 Defensive and >=80 Stress. The legacy score of 60.3 uses a different method. The previously published September 26 report retains its historical score of 63.36; this report's same-vintage September 25 observation is 63.77. Revisions are not treated as market changes.

Five- and 20-day returns are dashboard adjusted-price changes, not independently reconstructed dividend-reinvestment returns or strategy performance. Month-end breadth coverage was approximately 92.3% for the moving-average measure and 91.7% for the outperform measure. Breadth coverage and denominators vary; the AI sample contains only 28 stocks. Factor crowding dates differ: September 30 for the long-short ex-market variant, August 31 for beta-adjusted long-only. The screenshot's standalone WQS card labeled October 31 is not cited as an already observed current reading; the exported composite is retained without re-estimation. The original edition used decorative cover curves; this English cover uses brand imagery. Body charts use the original frozen inputs. 

## Disclosure
Prepared by Residual Inertia | 余势, author Taiyang Feng (Sunny), for research and information only. This is not investment advice. Reference exposure is not an actual-account allocation. The author's holdings and conflicts are not disclosed in this report. Historical results do not guarantee future performance.

- [2] [Massive adjusted-price methodology](https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/aggregates/custom-bars)
- [3] [New York Fed ACM Treasury Term Premia](https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/data_indicators/term-premia-tabs)
- [4] [Chicago Fed NFCI/ANFCI methodology](https://www.chicagofed.org/research/data/nfci/about)

The dashboard home figure is the simple mean of two September month-end ratios: 41.47% above the 200-day moving average (2,446/5,898) and 32.60% outperforming the SPY benchmark proxy over 12 months (1,863/5,715). Their average is 37.04%. The October 2 daily 200DMA estimate is separately 42.03% (2,449/5,827). The monthly figures use the Massive extension; they are not described as official CRSP observations. Different metrics and denominators prevent treating 37% to 42% as a five-point improvement.[1]

## AI hardware: strong, with heat and divergence
The composite scored 91.5 (Strong), with demand momentum 100.0, supply-chain confirmation 95.4, leadership breadth 81.2 and relative risk appetite 90.4. Crowding/heat at 81.5 and divergence fragility at 69.6 are risk measures, so higher is worse. SMH's 20-trading-day gain of 14.12% exceeded QQQ's 4.45% and SPY's -0.46% by 9.67 and 14.57 percentage points. In the 28-stock monitored universe, 25 stocks were above each of the 20-day and 50-day averages (89.3%). These are sector measures, not broad-market 200DMA breadth. AMD, TER and MRVL led the monitored universe over 20 days, gaining approximately 39.0%, 32.6% and 30.4%. A high composite score does not imply a low entry cost or continuing gains. Watch whether strength spreads as heat and divergence ease.[1][2]

## Rates: the answer depends on the window
As of October 1, the ACM 10-year fitted yield was 5.217%, comprising a 4.312% expected-average-short-rate component and a 0.905% term premium. Between September 1 and October 1, it rose 34.99 bp: 22.42 bp from the expected-rate component and 12.58 bp from the premium. Over three months, the premium contributed slightly more (36.23 bp versus 32.70 bp; total 68.93 bp). The expected-rate component accounted for approximately 64% of the one-month change; the term premium also rose. Rising long-end rates may increase valuation pressure, but this report does not identify an independent causal effect on equity returns. Expected rates contributed more over six months (60.33 versus 22.41 bp) and one year (75.90 versus 29.32 bp). These are model decompositions, not traded yield quotes or forecasts of the next FOMC decision.[3]

## Financial conditions and what to watch
The latest available NFCI and ANFCI observations, dated September 25, were -0.548 and -0.574. Both indicate looser-than-average conditions under their respective definitions; their 0.026 difference alone does not establish tightening.[1][4] Watch whether daily breadth improves alongside prices, participation and fragility ease, and AI hardware strength persists while heat and divergence cool.

## Version, methods and limitations
Published October 3, 2026. Equity/model cutoff: October 2; ACM: October 1; NFCI/ANFCI: September 25. The composite uses the dashboard's four-pillar rolling-percentile/equal-weight method; thresholds are <35 Constructive, 35-<50 Neutral, 50-<65 Caution, 65-<80 Defensive and >=80 Stress. The legacy score of 60.3 uses a different method. The previously published September 26 report retains its historical score of 63.36; this report's same-vintage September 25 observation is 63.77. Revisions are not treated as market changes.

Five- and 20-day returns are dashboard adjusted-price changes, not independently reconstructed dividend-reinvestment returns or strategy performance. Month-end breadth coverage was approximately 92.3% for the moving-average measure and 91.7% for the outperform measure. Breadth coverage and denominators vary; the AI sample contains only 28 stocks. Factor crowding dates differ: September 30 for the long-short ex-market variant, August 31 for beta-adjusted long-only. The screenshot's standalone WQS card labeled October 31 is not cited as an already observed current reading; the exported composite is retained without re-estimation. The original edition used decorative cover curves; this English cover uses brand imagery. Body charts use the original frozen inputs.
